core.title: Plan user/system flows as production orchestration, not test infrastructure
core.given: A user/system flow is involved in any planner artifact (plan, product capability, DESIRED OUTCOME, acceptance or doc)
core.when: the planner specifies, references or describes that user/system flow
core.then: Treat the user/system flow as production orchestration, not test infrastructure: located in the stack's production user/system flow directory and executed by the stack's production executor of a user/system flow.
prefer: Name the stack's production executor of a user/system flow as the executor.
Reference the stack's user/system flow implementation-patterns documentation as the place where user/system flow implementation patterns are described.
avoid: Planning user/system flows as test infrastructure (fixtures, harnesses, test-only helpers) or placing them under test directories.
Stating an executor or location for user/system flows other than the stack's production executor in the production user/system flow directory.
core.why: User/system flows are production orchestration executed by the stack's production executor in the production user/system flow directory; classifying them as test infrastructure misstates what they are and where they live.
evidence: Planner artifacts involving a user/system flow treat it as production code in the production user/system flow directory, executed by the production executor of a user/system flow.
No planner artifact describes a user/system flow as test infrastructure or locates it under a test path.
verification: The check verifies location and executor: the expected location is the production user/system flow directory and the expected executor is the production executor of a user/system flow (with its entry-point module); the concrete directory, executor name and entry point are supplied by the profile when the core is realized.

The expected user/system-flow-patterns reference is the stack's designated user/system flow implementation-patterns document (a profile location); lineage annotations carried on the reference (e.g. a session marker) are realization metadata, not part of the obligation.

Activation requires train-specific context (a user/system flow term, the executor's name, or a user/system flow artifact/location); generic orchestration terms or plan-path signals alone are supporting signals only and never activate the rule on their own.
The planning-phase fact scopes the audience (planner authoring artifacts) only; it is not a narrowing condition on the obligation.
Whether an artifact frames or places a user/system flow as test infrastructure rather than production code requires judgement; it is not decided from paths alone.

A term alias binding the executor's local name to the concept 'the production executor of a user/system flow' is realization data; the core refers only to the concept, whose concrete name is a profile value.

values: file under the production user/system flow directory
user/system flow framed or placed as test infrastructure

fires: Any planner artifact (plan, product capability, DESIRED OUTCOME, acceptance, doc) that involves a user/system flow, whether or not it explicitly discusses placement or executor.
A plan proposes putting user/system flow orchestration under a test directory or describes it as test fixtures/harness.
Docs for a user/system flow name an executor or location other than the stack's production executor in the production user/system flow directory.
doesNotFire: Planner artifacts with no user/system flow involved, even if they use generic words like 'orchestration' or live under a plan path.
Acceptance tests that exercise a user/system flow are themselves test code; the rule still applies to how the user/system flow they exercise is classified.

The specific document where the stack's user/system flow implementation patterns are documented; instantiates the core's 'user/system flow implementation-patterns documentation' in prefer[1] and verification. (The conventions tree root is roots.conventions; this rule does not need it.)

neutralityNotes: User/system flow, product capability and DESIRED OUTCOME are ATDD methodology vocabulary (user-system-flow/capability/desired-outcome are urn artifact params in the closed vocabulary) and are kept in the core; they are not stack specifics. Everything concrete is carried by four closed-vocabulary profile keys: the production user/system flow directory and the user/system flow executor (roles.runtime_components map entries), the user/system-flow-artifact naming (suffix.user-system-flow) and the specific user/system-flow-patterns document (layout.locations map entry); the conventions tree root (roots.conventions) is not needed by this rule, and the (SESSION-12) lineage annotation on the patterns document is realization metadata and stays Bun-only. activation.facts[1] is a path_glob in bun.json, but the neutral fact vocabulary has no path_glob, so it is expressed as a file_kind fact whose concrete patterns come from the profile. The term id user_system_flow_runner is a realization detail and remains Bun-only. Profile substitution of the concrete directory, executor and document is described in core verification as realization machinery only; bun.json imposes no requirement on how a checker implementation obtains those values, and none was added. 'unless' is empty in bun.json and stays empty; no exception was dropped or added.
